title: Kajjayya
description: Traditional festive sweet made from soaked raw rice and jaggery paaka, flavored with cardamom, roasted sesame seeds, and dry coconut.

steps.instruction: Wash the rice and soak in water for 3 days. Be sure to change the water every morning.
On the day of making, drain the rice and spread on a dry cotton cloth for 30 minutes. The rice must stay slightly moist — not bone dry.
Powder the rice to chiroti rava consistency. Keep covered with a moist cloth so it retains hydration.
Paaka: Add jaggery and water to a heavy pot over medium–high heat. Bring to a rolling boil.
Paaka test: drop a little into water on a plate. If it flows when tilted, cook further. If it solidifies into a soft ball and does not flow, it is ready.
Lower heat to medium; stir in roasted sesame, poppy seeds, dry coconut, and cardamom.
Add rice powder gradually while stirring continuously to avoid lumps. Cook on medium for 5 minutes until dough is soft yet firm.
Cool dough for 20–30 minutes until comfortable to handle. Shape lemon-sized portions, flatten on greased sheet, and deep-fry in medium-hot oil.
When kajjayya floats, flip to brown evenly. Remove when tan-brown and press gently to drain excess oil.

storyOrOrigin: An ancient Karnataka festive delicacy prepared for Deepavali and major family rituals, famed for its tender crumb and rich jaggery sweetness.
grandmasSecrets: Getting the paaka right is the most important thing. Have everything ready — once the jaggery reaches the right stage you must work fast.
Keep the pounded rice covered with a moist cloth; if it dries out, the kajjayya will break in oil.
